findings.problem: The Definitions file marks only `mapPt_coe` as @[simp]. There is no canonical simp lemma that composes two `mapPt`s, i.e. `mapPt β hβ (mapPt α hα P) = mapPt (α ≫ β) _ P`, and no extensionality lemma for `mapPt` with a given composite. The proof therefore proves a general statement locally as `comp_eq`, with three side-condition hypotheses plus `α ≫ β = γ`. It then applies it by hand through `rw [comp_eq ...]` at n11, n12, n21, n22 and hχφ. Each use re-supplies the five-argument shape. Because the identity is not registered, `simp` cannot normalise nested `mapPt` terms such as `mapPt χ hχ (mapPt φ1 hφ1 P)` in the goals at lines 90–92. The user has to rewrite with `← hχφ` and `rw [hχφ]` explicitly. Other files nest `mapPt φ hφ (mapPt φ hφ P)` in statements, so the missing rule is a library-level gap and not a local one.
findings.proposed_change: In Def_CerednikDrinfeld_QMModuli.lean, next to `mapPt_coe`, add a lemma `mapPt_mapPt` (or `mapPt_comp`) stating `mapPt β hβ (mapPt α hα P) = mapPt (α ≫ β) (by rw [Category.assoc, hβ, hα]) P`, proved by `Subtype.ext (by simp [Category.assoc])`. Mark it @[simp], oriented toward the single composite so that it terminates and every nested `mapPt` collapses to a normal form. Optionally add `mapPt_ext`, to turn equality of points into equality of the underlying morphisms. Then `comp_eq` becomes a one-line corollary: `rw [mapPt_mapPt, h]` plus proof-irrelevance. The `simp only [mapPt_coe] at this` step at line 96 can use the same rule.
findings.benefit: Composition of pushforwards on points is stated and normalised once. Every proof about isogeny compositions can then use `simp` or one `rw` instead of re-deriving the 12-binder `comp_eq`. Nested `mapPt` expressions get a single canonical form. This file's n11–n22 and hχφ steps become shorter and less error-prone.
